Kept, not shown wrong.

grade_rationale.text: Afanasyev records the baba-yaga for Belarusians, Russians, Little Russians (Ukrainians), Slovaks and Serbs.
Ralston describes the Baba Yaga of the Russian popular tales, her mortar and the White-Russian fiery mortar without citing Afanasyev on these passages, so he counts as an independent source for them.
Ralston records the Servian Baba Yaga, the Iron Tooth, without citing Afanasyev on that passage.
Ralston's White-Russian passage on Death and the souls of the dead cites Afanasyev (Skazki I.120), so it is counted once with Afanasyev.
Ralston's etymology note in Russian Folk-Tales quotes Afanasyev, so it is not independent of him.
Machal, a third author, records Jaga-baba and Jezibaba in Polish fairy-tales; the identification with this creature rests on the name forms and is flagged.
